title: Friday Sermon 68: Adam's Names, Remembrance, Code 19, and Libya (1982-12-17)
date_note: Explicit in the filename. The first twenty minutes are severely unintelligible.
source_file: data/sources/playlists/audio-transcripts/68 - Friday Sermon 17 Dec. 1982 By Dr. Rashad Khalifa.csv
document_summary: A difficult recording whose opening sermon is largely unintelligible. From approximately twenty minutes onward, Dean Mahmoud returns to Quran 2:31 and argues that the names taught to Adam may be God's names or qualities, especially knowledge that all power comes from God. Satan's temptation causes humanity to forget the source of delegated power. Revelation, remembrance, prayer, Quran 2:286, and Quran 33:41 counteract forgetfulness. After prayer, the discussion becomes fragmented around scholarly authority, the nineteen-letter Bismillah, wahid, Deedat, Baha'i uses of nineteen, and religious additions. The final section introduces an Algerian visitor, Dean's 1977 Algeria trip, Rashad's education and employment, his period as Gaddafi's science adviser, the origins of his rejection of Hadith, and conflicting assessments of Gaddafi and Libya.

sections.summary: A visiting Algerian participant speaks with Dean and Rashad about Algeria and Mostaganem. Rashad summarizes studying and teaching in California, industrial research at Monsanto, serving for two years as Gaddafi's science adviser, and joining the United Nations. He recounts a national billboard falsely labeled as Hadith and calls it the beginning of his rejection of Hadith. Participants debate propaganda and Gaddafi's writings, while Rashad describes him as a dictator who turned Libya into a prison.
